author: WP21
summary: A short appendix on the experimental native C API: ABI 0.29.0 and its independence from the product version, results and thread-local errors, handles and ownership, strings and callbacks, the generated coverage inventory, route families, packaging and the release gate. Mostly current (the modules/c-api tree is unchanged since the source's pin), but it calls the headers C17, understates the buffer protocol, omits that no route offers a thread queue, and its gate account needs the measured two-unmet result. libcna.com already covered the build, history, programming model and internals in depth; two reference deep dives now carry the contract residue (admission, buffers, retention, device lifetimes, route families) and the evidence and gate semantics.

concepts.text: The native C surface at TARGET has 61 public headers and 4,055 exported cna_* routes, and its ABI version (0.29.0, encoded 0x00001D00; alpha.1 exported 0.7.0) is independent of the CNA product version, which is still 0.1.0-alpha.1.
concepts.note: The source calls it a 'C17 ABI'; the public headers are held to a C99 consumer floor (see WP21-appi-004).

concepts.text: The alpha.1 compile blocker (the C renderer-identity table checked against the C++ identity count by a static_assert, 49 rows against 50) is historical: at TARGET the table has 25 rows for 25 identities and MAXIMUM equals the highest published value, so both assertions hold by inspection; whether the library builds at TARGET is not verified.
concepts.note: Positive evidence of the fix is by reading; a syntax-only compile of the translation unit was run for the Known Issues verification (CNA-BUG-059 proven fixed there). No build of the library.

concepts.text: TARGET's C ABI release gate is NOT READY, and running it measures the coverage-closed and limitations-matrix criteria as unmet because the runtime-scope model of the coverage generator does not classify the design, diagnostics and inspector modules; this is a current generated-inventory defect, unrelated to the old compile blocker.
concepts.note: The committed RELEASE_GATE.md still reads '1 criteria are unmet'; docs/c-api.html#status and docs/verification.html#coverage-reports quote that record (errata item 51). CNA-BUG-062.

concepts.text: The public C headers use only fixed-width integers, POD structures, opaque 64-bit handles, function pointers and caller-owned buffers; no exception, template, STL type, C++ object layout or allocator ownership crosses the boundary. They are held to a C99 consumer floor (23 declared cells across 7 toolchains, C++ cells up to c++23 optional), while CNA's own C test targets compile at C17.
concepts.note: The source says headers compile as strict C17 and C++23; TARGET's declared floor is C99 (required cc c99/c11/c17 and c++ c++11/14/17 cells), with c23/c++23 only in optional cells.

concepts.text: A consumer checks the ABI generation first with cna_get_abi_version(), which returns the constant compiled into the library and needs no runtime. Refusing only an older library (runtime < CNA_ABI_VERSION) admits every newer 0.x minor, including the incompatible 0.28.0 and 0.29.0, and even a new major; CMake's SameMajorVersion package check and the never-bumped ELF node CNA_C_API_0.1 cannot tell minors apart, a removed route (cna_sprite_batch_draw_mesh_ext) fails only when the dynamic linker binds it, and a contract change passes both. Binding authors should require one ABI version, query capabilities, obey the ownership rules and keep a consumer test per platform.

concepts.note: The source's listing refuses only an older library; the page shows what that admits and gives a strict check (syntax-checked).

concepts.text: While the ABI is 0.x an incompatible change increments the minor and regenerates the symbol/layout baseline, additive generations also get a minor a consumer can require, and renderer identity values that remain are stable while retired values are never reused (the next new identity takes 52).

concepts.text: Every fallible call returns a fixed-width CNA_Result (0 success to 14 buffer too small); a failure records a structured error and UTF-8 message for the calling thread, read with count-then-copy routes; C++ exceptions are converted by a positional exception barrier, and a lifecycle-callback failure is latched through CNA_CallbackError, stops the game at a safe point and reports CNA_RESULT_CALLBACK. The declared CNA_RESULT_SHUTTING_DOWN is returned by no route at TARGET.
concepts.note: The source lists a 'shutdown' failure category as if returned; no route in modules/c-api/src returns CNA_RESULT_SHUTTING_DOWN (only ErrorCategoryForResult maps it).

target.evidence: modules/c-api/include/CNA/C/abi.h (CNA_Result codes); modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiDetail.hpp (CallWithExceptionBarrier); modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiDetail.cpp (Fail, LastError); modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiRuntime.cpp (RecordCallbackFailure)

concepts.text: CNA_Handle packs a table slot and a generation; a zero, stale, recycled or wrong-kind handle answers CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE and a foreign thread CNA_RESULT_THREAD before any C++ object is touched. At TARGET there is one process-wide registry that checks slot, generation, kind and creation thread; handles are process-local values, never pointers or serialized IDs.
concepts.note: The source (and CNA's HANDLES.md) say the registry also checks the owning runtime and ownership state; the code has no separate runtime identity (one registry per process) and resolves ownership per family.

concepts.text: Each handle parameter or result names one of six ownership categories (owned, borrowed, retained, transferred, callback context, caller buffer); owned game children must be destroyed before the game, and cna_game_destroy refuses with INVALID_STATE while a counted child lives instead of leaving dangling pointers; one C-owned game is active per process.

A SpriteBatch bulk submission retains every referenced texture until cna_sprite_batch_end succeeds; texture destruction answers INVALID_STATE meanwhile, a failing native End leaves the batch in its interval with textures retained, and destroying the batch is the recovery that drops deferred commands and releases the references. Textures from another game are refused with INVALID_HANDLE before anything is retained.

Handles returned by typed content loads are separate owned game children: cna_content_manager_unload only clears the native manager cache and neither unload nor manager destruction releases handles already issued, so they stay valid; the game's own borrowed manager cannot be destroyed.
concepts.note: By reading; no test uses a loaded resource after unloading its manager.

concepts.text: Resources on a caller-created device (cna_graphics_device_create) do not gate cna_game_destroy and, per the header, are released with the device: cna_graphics_device_destroy disposes and releases without a child count, the C++ layer disposes tracked resources, but their handles stay registered and the header does not say whether they must still be destroyed; the order is untested. cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device fails for such resources.
concepts.note: Extends the source's 'runtime shutdown refuses unsafe live-child states': the caller-created device is the exception. Corrects site statements that child-first order is the caller's obligation there (errata item 52); B9 NEW-B9-01 and NEW-B9-14.

concepts.text: Graphics and game-child handles are creation-thread-affine and a wrong-thread call answers CNA_RESULT_THREAD; at TARGET no route documents a deferred-release or dispatch queue, and although the streaming-audio header says buffer submission is safe from a producer thread, cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer resolves its handle through the same thread-checked registry lookup.
concepts.note: The source allows an exception for 'a route that documents a safe submission queue'; none exists, and the one route whose documentation claims producer-thread use is thread-checked (issue WP21-i001).

target.evidence: modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiAudio.cpp (cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer, BorrowDynamicInstance, GetSoundEffectInstance); modules/c-api/src/CnaCApiDetail.hpp (HandleRegistry::Get creation-thread check); docs/c-api/AUDIO.md; docs/c-api/CALLBACKS_AND_THREADING.md

concepts.text: Variable-length output uses a size-then-copy pair into caller memory: a null destination with nonzero capacity is INVALID_ARGUMENT, a null destination with zero capacity reports the required count (BUFFER_TOO_SMALL unless it is zero), and a too-small buffer receives nothing at all while the full required count is reported; counts exclude any terminator and CNA never allocates an output for the caller.
concepts.note: The source says no partial UTF-8 character is written; TARGET writes no partial data at all (all-or-nothing).

concepts.text: UTF-8 inputs are borrowed pointer-plus-length views validated before conversion (NULL only with length 0; embedded U+0000 refused with CNA_RESULT_ENCODING for paths, names, titles and identifiers); arrays pair a pointer with a uint64_t count whose unit the route names, are overflow-checked, and are read during the call only unless the route copies them (PCM creation, streaming submission, the renderer fallback chain).

Versioned input structures start with struct_size and struct_version; the routes read at TARGET accept struct_size >= sizeof(current) with struct_version == 1 and refuse a smaller prefix, so callers zero the structure and set both fields.
concepts.note: The source mentions only struct_size; TARGET also requires struct_version.

concepts.text: Callback tables are copied at registration (cna_game_create copies CNA_GameCallbacks) while the functions and the caller-owned context must stay valid until the registration is destroyed or its source has been destroyed; event subscriptions are owned registration handles; callback-scoped game and device handles are borrowed, generation-invalidated after the callback, and cannot be kept as owned objects.
concepts.note: Synchronisation of registration removal with an in-flight invocation is CNA's documented contract; not traced per family.

concepts.text: The C ABI covers runtime core and math, the game lifecycle, graphics and renderer selection, content and CNB, input, audio, media, devices and sensors, GamerServices, networking and storage, and the CNAEXT engine layer (886 routes); the page groups all 61 headers by family with their route counts summing to 4,055.

C callers enumerate the identities compiled into the build and query renderer features instead of inferring support from a name, and choose the renderer process-wide before the first device exists: after creation the selection is latched, setters answer INVALID_STATE, get_active answers INVALID_STATE until then, and fallback records carry one of four reasons.

Resource routes use typed handles and validate same-game and same-device relationships: each resource keeps its owner token and cross-device or cross-game use is refused; the surface spans textures, buffers, render targets, SpriteBatch, state, effects, models, animation and engine-layer resources at the completion recorded by the inventory.

The pure-C tests are compiled unchanged into whichever renderer tree is configured and accept each renderer's answer: HEADLESS establishes handles, errors and lifetimes but no pixels, a 2D renderer answers NOT_SUPPORTED for 3D resources. CNA declares four run configurations (HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER, SOFTWARE, SOFTWARE with sanitizers), but no tool, preset or workflow configures them; tests needing a GL context use SDL_VIDEODRIVER=x11 with CNA_TEST_DISPLAY.
concepts.note: The source says tests run against more than one renderer; TARGET only declares the four trees, and no CI job runs any.

concepts.text: Audio handles cover PCM effects and instances, streaming instances (the same handle kind as ordinary instances), index-addressed microphones and XACT engines, banks, categories and cues; device, media, storage, GamerServices and networking routes follow the same handle, thread and error rules, and partial mappings stay partial (15 approved rows, e.g. GameServiceContainer::GetService served by cna_game_services_contains_ext).

The C API installs shared and static libraries, a package config and an ABI-derived version file (component CNACApi, CNA::CApi, CNA::CApiStatic); CApi_InstalledConsumer builds and runs a strict-C program from the installed prefix (Linux/ELF, local only); header compatibility is declared as 23 cells across 7 toolchains and compiled by the compat workflow; the WebAssembly artifact exports the C symbols with a JavaScript-owned loop contract and its own tests.

issues.text: cna_dynamic_sound_effect_instance_submit_buffer (and the float variant) are documented as safe to call from a producer thread, but resolve the instance through the creation-thread-checked registry, so another thread gets CNA_RESULT_THREAD.
MODULE_SCOPE leaves design, diagnostics and inspector unclassified; the coverage, limitations, scope-model and release-gate checks fail at TARGET.
LIMITATIONS.md partitions 8,887 of 9,355 declarations and omits the 468 planned rows; the release note still attributes 654 declarations to CBIND-117.
Destroying a caller-created GraphicsDevice before its resources is permitted by the header but untested; handle obligations afterwards are unspecified.
cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device fails for resources created on a caller-created device (the owner token is treated as a game).
No CI job builds the C library or runs its tests; the four declared run configurations are configured by no preset, script or workflow, and six release-gate criteria are presence checks.
CNA_RESULT_SHUTTING_DOWN is documented (HANDLES.md) for a closing/closed runtime but no route returns it.

Stale C API prose: cnb.h's file comment says the document, schemas and loader registry are not published yet; FEATURE_MATRIX.md says ABI 0.1.0, 14 capability flags, compile-time-only renderer selection and 50 identities; the CApiReleaseGate CMake comment speaks of two open packaging decisions.
No test uses a content-loaded C handle after its manager's Unload or destruction, although the contract says it stays valid.
